NVIDIA just saved 30 years of animation tech.

they open-sourced a model that generates 350,000 motion skills in real-time, at 15,000 fps with 2ms latency. https://t.co/3Lgs8aMJtx

it's called MotionBricks, a framework built to generate real-time character and humanoid motion at scale. zero mocap, zero rigging, no animation graph. you describe the movement, the network generates every frame.

here's the repo: https://t.co/ENLD93j7Ik
it's already wired into NVIDIA's GR00T robotics stack, so the same model that animates a game character can drive a real humanoid. games and robots, 1 motion brain.

motion stops being the bottleneck, and the interface around it becomes the thing players actually judge. the movement is solved, the game still has to look like a game.

this is what i use to generate clean game UI mockups for any genre:

https://t.co/9EmRHjV5rX

follow if you're building with AI and want the whole thing looking shipped, not just the parts that move.
